plain: The art of speaking clearly and well in public.

webster.text: Pronunciation; the utterance or delivery of words, particularly in public discourses and arguments.

more.text: In ancient treatises on oratory, the wording of a discourse; the choice and order of words; composition; the act of framing a writing or discourse.

example.quote: President, and some others, members of this respectable Convention, — whose profound oratory and elocution would, on the journals of a British House of Commons, stand as lasting monuments of their great abilities, — a man of my circumscribed scale of talents is not adequate to the task of contending with ;
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 4, South Carolina Convention, Mr. ALEXANDER TWEED, May 20, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
